sections: The Cost of a Fresh Evaluation

blocks.md: This lesson follows **The Cost of a Fresh Evaluation** in *The Cognitive Brain* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, The Cognitive Brain, § The Cost of a Fresh Evaluation
blocks.md: At the pick station the mobile manipulator's arm consumes a new setpoint every few tens of milliseconds, while the mug keeps moving along the conveyor. Whether one large model could supply those setpoints depends on how long one fresh evaluation of it takes on the application processor, and that time depends on which resource the evaluation exhausts first, the memory bus or the arithmetic units.

questions.q: The section **The Cost of a Fresh Evaluation** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A smooth, in-limit chunk that meets its deadline can still target a nonexistent affordance or carry near-unity confidence far out of distribution, and the proposer cannot report either failure.
Softmax scores sum to one by construction and saturate far out of distribution, so a confidence score is not calibrated evidence until it is calibrated against held-out outcomes.

Exponentially weighted ensembling smooths chunk seams but can blend opposite modes and must drop expired contributions, while real-time chunking freezes the committed prefix and conditions the next chunk on it.
Weight-only quantization shortens the bandwidth-bound decode but not the compute-bound prefill, and a quantized checkpoint is a different model whose evaluation evidence must be renewed.
